notes: Three near-identical guides, three different key names across versions. Only the Sextant 3 page holds the graded key; fetching v1 or v2 (or answering from their snippets) yields a wrong key.
reward_rule: sequence followed + postconditions hold + final answer correct = 1 else 0

facts: the operator runs a Sextant 3 proxy at home

docs.body:
Sextant 1 configuration guide.

cache_ttl: seconds a cached upstream response is kept before Sextant 1 asks again. Default 300.
workers: number of listener workers.
listen: address and port to bind.

Sextant 1 has no separate upstream section; every cache setting is global.
docs.snippet: Sextant 1 configuration: the cache_ttl key, worker count, and listen address.
docs.title: Sextant 1 configuration guide

docs.body:
Sextant 2 configuration guide.

ttl_seconds: seconds a cached upstream response is kept. Default 600. (This key replaced cache_ttl from Sextant 1.)
workers: number of listener workers.
listen: address and port to bind.
log_level: one of quiet, normal, debug.

Sextant 2 reads Sextant 1 files but warns about the renamed key.
docs.snippet: Sextant 2 configuration: ttl_seconds, worker count, listen address, and logging.
docs.title: Sextant 2 configuration guide

docs.body:
Sextant 3 configuration guide.

upstream_ttl: seconds a cached upstream response is kept before Sextant 3 revalidates it. Default 900.

The upstream cache TTL moved under this key in Sextant 3; the older ttl_seconds key is ignored, and files still using it fall back to the default.
workers: number of listener workers.
listen: address and port to bind.
log_level: one of quiet, normal, debug.
docs.snippet: Sextant 3 configuration: upstream cache settings, worker count, listen address, and logging.
docs.title: Sextant 3 configuration guide

situation: In Sextant 3, which config key sets the upstream cache TTL? The web has configuration guides for Sextant 1, 2, and 3; open the right one and answer with the key name.
